# Comwit Template — agent guide

`create-comwit` scaffolds a Next.js 16 project whose structure is the documentation:
services sliced by domain, four layers that depend one way, an `.ai.md` rulebook beside
every layer, and skills for the one-time setups. Two positions: AI-native (the rules an
agent needs ship with the project) and Next.js as the full stack (the api layer is the
backend).

## Create a project

```bash
npm create comwit@latest my-app     # or: npx create-comwit@latest my-app
cd my-app && pnpm run dev
```

Flags: `--opennext` (Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext: wrangler.jsonc, open-next.config.ts, `preview`/`deploy` scripts) ·
`--name <pkg>` · `--pm pnpm|npm|yarn|bun` · `--no-install` · `--no-git` · `--dry`.

## Inside a generated project

Read these before writing code, in this order:

1. `AGENTS.md` — the rules file (CLAUDE.md imports it): flow, stack, tree, env, database/storage/deploy.
2. `src/services/.ai.md` — import rules and layer dependencies.
3. The `.ai.md` of the layer you are about to touch: `src/services/api.ai.md`,
   `src/services/state.ai.md`, `src/services/page.ai.md`, `src/server/repository/.ai.md`,
   `src/app/.ai.md`, `src/services/admin/.ai.md`.
4. `src/services/design.md` before any visual decision.

Dependency flow `page → state → api → repository`; write order is the reverse. All data
goes through `src/server/repository/` (in-memory rows in `_data/` until a database is
connected; connecting one changes only repository bodies). The api layer's `'use server'`
functions are wrapped in `createAction` and exported through `resolveActions`; the build
turns them into the kit's own transport (one POST route handler, parallel calls, only
`ActionError` messages reach the browser), not native Server Actions — keep the source
convention and call the api only through a domain's `index.ts`.

Skills in `.agents/skills/`: `app-setup` (tabs, detail screens, PWA — before the first app
screen), `auth-setup` (Better Auth per service — after a database), `seo-optimize`,
`pnpm run validate` after every change; the
Oxlint rules in `eslint-rules/` enforce every boundary above.
